publications.title: Neural Emulators for Dark Matter Halo Mass Functions at z > 2
publications.abstract: We train neural network emulators on a suite of N-body simulations to predict halo mass functions at z > 2 with sub-percent accuracy, enabling rapid cosmological inference without repeated simulation runs.

publications.title: The Λ-CDM Tension in Recent H₀ Measurements: A Bayesian Reanalysis
publications.abstract: We perform a Bayesian reanalysis of H₀ tension combining Planck 2018 CMB measurements with low-redshift distance ladder constraints. Our analysis reveals systematic offsets not captured by standard ΛCDM error budgets.

publications.title: Gravitational Wave Standard Sirens and the Hubble Constant: Constraints from Binary Neutron Star Mergers
publications.abstract: We derive H₀ constraints from binary neutron star merger GW events, using electromagnetic counterparts as host galaxy identifiers. Independent of distance ladder calibrations, our result is consistent with both Planck and SH0ES values.

publications.title: Baryonic Feedback in Halo Models: Constraints from Weak Lensing Power Spectra
Galaxy Cluster Counts from Combined SZ and X-ray Surveys: Cosmological Implications
publications.abstract: We combine cluster catalogs from the South Pole Telescope SZ survey and eROSITA X-ray survey to constrain Ωm and σ₈. The joint analysis reduces parameter uncertainties by 35% compared to either survey alone.

publications.title: Primordial Non-Gaussianity Constraints from the CMB Bispectrum in Single-Field Inflation
Gravitational waves of quasicircular, inspiraling black hole binaries in an ultralight vector-dark-matter environment
publications.abstract: The gravitational waves emitted by massive black hole binaries can be affected by a variety of environmental effects, which, if detected, could inform astrophysics and cosmology. We here study how gravitational waves emitted by black holes in quasicircular orbits are affected by the presence of an ultralight, vector field, dark-matter environment that is minimally coupled to the binary. This dark-matter environment induces oscillatory gravitational potentials that perturb the orbit of the binary, leaving an imprint in the binary’s binding energy, and thus on the gravitational waves emitted. We here compute the effect of this environment on the gravitational wave phase using the stationary-phase approximation within the post-Newtonian formalism. We then perform a Fisher analysis to estimate the detectability of this environmental effect with a four-year Laser Interferometric Space Antenna (LISA) observation, focusing on vector fields with ultralight masses in the <math display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>eV</mi></mrow></math> range. We conclude that the observation of such gravitational waves with spaceborne interferometers, like LISA, could yield a measurement or constraint on local, vector dark-matter environments, provided the dark-matter density is larger than roughly <math display="inline"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>14</mn></msup><msub><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">⊙</mo></msub><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>pc</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>.

publications.title: Light-Cone N-body Simulations for Next-Generation Cosmological Surveys
Constraints on σ₈ from CMB-Lensing × Galaxy-Survey Cross-Correlations
publications.abstract: We cross-correlate CMB lensing maps from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope with galaxy overdensity maps from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3, obtaining a 3.1σ constraint on σ₈ that is in mild tension with Planck ΛCDM predictions.

publications.title: Cosmological perturbations with ultralight vector dark matter fields: Numerical implementation in class
publications.abstract: In this work we consider a dark matter candidate described by an ultralight vector field, whose mass is in principle in the range <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>eq</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∼</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>eV</mi><mo>≪</mo><mi>m</mi><mo><</mo><mi>eV</mi></mrow></math>. The homogeneous background vector field is assumed to point in a given direction. We present a numerical implementation of cosmological perturbations in a Bianchi type I geometry with vector field dark matter in a modified version of the Cosmic Linear Anisotropy Solving System. We study the evolution of large-scale cosmological perturbations in the linear regime. We compute the matter power spectrums defined for Fourier modes pointing in a given direction. We obtain interesting features in the power spectrums whose observational significance depends on the field mass. We compare the results with the standard <math display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi></math> cold dark matter and with the corresponding well-studied ultralight scalar field dark matter case. As for the scalar case we obtain a suppression in the power spectrums at small scales characterized by the same scale, namely the Jeans scale. The main characteristic feature of the vector field model we notice here for first time is that the amplitude of the suppression effect depends on the direction of the Fourier modes with respect to the background vector field, leaving eventually a possible anisotropic imprint in structure formation at small scales.

publications.title: Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Detection Prospects for LISA
Subhalo Abundance Matching Revisited: WDM versus CDM at Sub-Galactic Scales
publications.abstract: We revisit subhalo abundance matching predictions for warm dark matter (WDM) models against Milky Way satellite counts, finding that WDM particle masses below 3.5 keV are in tension with observed subhalo populations.

publications.title: A Bayesian Reassessment of the Distance Ladder and H₀ Tension
publications.abstract: We construct a hierarchical Bayesian model of the distance ladder incorporating Cepheid, Tip of the Red Giant Branch, and Type Ia supernova calibrators. Our simultaneous fit yields H₀ = 71.5 ± 1.3 km/s/Mpc, partially alleviating the tension with Planck.

publications.title: Ultralight vector dark matter, anisotropies, and cosmological adiabatic modes
publications.abstract: In this work we study the background evolution and the early time behavior of scalar cosmological perturbations with an ultralight vector dark matter. We present a model for vector dark matter in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe. Vector fields source anisotropies in the early Universe characterized by a shear tensor which rapidly decays once the fields start oscillating, making them viable dark matter candidates. We present the set of equations needed to evolve scalar cosmological perturbations in the linear regime, both in synchronous gauge and Newtonian gauge. We show that the shear tensor has to be taken into account in the calculation of adiabatic initial conditions.

publications.title: Intrinsic Alignment Models for Weak Gravitational Lensing: A Comparative Study
publications.abstract: We compare five intrinsic alignment (IA) models against data from DES Y3 cosmic shear, finding that the nonlinear alignment model with tidal torquing corrections best describes galaxy shape correlations at separations below 10 Mpc/h.

publications.title: Intrinsic Alignments in Stage-IV Surveys: Challenges and Mitigation Strategies
publications.abstract: Conference proceedings summarising current challenges in modelling and mitigating intrinsic alignment contamination in weak lensing analyses targeting Stage-IV surveys such as LSST and Euclid.

publications.title: Rényi entropies of the massless Dirac field on the torus
publications.abstract: We compute the Rényi entropies of the massless Dirac field on the Euclidean torus (the Lorentzian cylinder at nonzero temperature) for arbitrary spatial regions. We do it by the resolvent method, i.e., we express the entropies in terms of the resolvent of a certain operator and then use the explicit form of that resolvent, which was obtained recently. Our results are different in appearance from those already existing in the literature (obtained via the replica trick), but they agree perfectly, as we show numerically for noninteger order and analytically for integer order. We also compute the Rényi mutual information, and find that, for appropriate choices of the parameters, it is nonpositive and nonmonotonic. This behavior is expected, but it cannot be seen with the simplest known Rényi entropies in quantum field theory because they are proportional to the entanglement entropy.
